t.6.101.1: Thus instructed, Hanūmān, the son of Māruta, entered the city of Laṅkā, being honored by the night-wanderers.
t.6.101.2: Entering Rāvaṇa's dwelling, the greatly radiant one saw her, like Rohiṇī bereft of the moon and filled with dread.
t.6.101.3: Quiet, bowed low and humble, he approached her and, having greeted her respectfully, began to relate all the words of Rāma.
t.6.101.4: O Vaidehī, Rāma is well, together with Sugrīva and Lakṣmaṇa; and that subduer of foes, his purpose accomplished and his enemy slain, asks after your welfare.
t.6.101.5: O queen, Rāvaṇa has been slain by Rāma, who had Vibhīṣaṇa as his ally, together with the monkeys, and through the sound counsel of Lakṣmaṇa.
t.6.101.6: And the heroic Rāma, delight of the Raghus, having asked after your welfare, spoke to you, supremely pleased, with his inner self fulfilled.
t.6.101.7: O queen, I tell you pleasing news, and I congratulate you once more: by good fortune you live, O knower of dharma, through my victory in battle.
t.6.101.8: Victory has been won by us, Sītā; be at ease, free from distress. That enemy Rāvaṇa has been slain, and this Laṅkā stands under our control.
t.6.101.9: For I, who found no sleep and stayed resolute in the struggle to win you back, have fulfilled this vow by building a bridge across the great ocean.
t.6.101.11: Therefore take heart, be at ease; you are now as if in your own home. And he comes here, overjoyed, eager to see you.
t.6.101.10: And no alarm should be felt by you, though you are dwelling in Rāvaṇa's abode, for this sovereignty of Laṅkā has been placed under the command of Vibhīṣaṇa.
t.6.101.12: Thus addressed, Sītā, whose face was like the moon, sprang up; overcome by joy, she could not utter a single word.
t.6.101.13: And the best of monkeys said to Sītā, who made no reply: "What are you thinking about, O queen, and why do you not speak to me?"
t.6.101.14: Thus addressed by Hanumān, Sītā, steadfast in dharma, supremely delighted, spoke in a voice choked with joy.
t.6.101.15: Having heard this welcome news concerning my husband's victory, I was overcome by joy and for a moment I am left without words.
t.6.101.16: Though I keep pondering, O monkey, I truly see nothing here that would be a fitting reward for you, who have brought me these tidings so dear to me.
t.6.101.17: And I see nothing on this earth, gentle one, O monkey, that would be fitting and equal to give you in return for your telling me this news so dear to me.
t.6.101.19: Thus addressed by Vaidehī, the monkey, standing before Sītā with joined palms held in reverence, replied with these words.
t.6.101.18: Gold or silver, jewels of many kinds, or even sovereignty over the three worlds: none of this is worthy to match the words you have spoken.
t.6.101.20: O lady devoted to what is dear and beneficial to your husband, O you who long for your husband's victory, you alone are worthy to speak such affectionate words.
t.6.101.21: O gentle lady, these words of yours, full of substance and affection, surpass even a heap of various jewels and the kingship of the gods.
t.6.101.23: But if you permit it, I wish to kill all these rākṣasīs by whom you were threatened before.
t.6.101.22: Indeed, in substance I have attained such blessings as sovereignty over the gods, since I see Rāma standing victorious, his enemy slain.
t.6.101.24: Those cruel women, dreadful in form and conduct and with eyes crueler still, who harassed you while you suffered in the Aśoka grove, you who revere your husband as a god...
t.6.101.25: These rākṣasīs of cruel speech, grant me this boon concerning them: I wish to slay these exceedingly cruel ones with blows of many kinds.
t.6.101.26: With fists and with hands, and with feet too, O lovely lady, with terrible blows of the knees and by the knocking out of their teeth
t.6.101.28: O glorious queen, I wish to kill these women who have wronged you with many such kinds of torments.
t.6.101.27: By biting off their ears and noses, likewise by tearing out their hair, and by dreadful trampling and blows, these women, their faces utterly dried up, would be struck down.
t.6.101.29: Thus addressed by Hanumān, the illustrious Vaidehī, daughter of Janaka, spoke to Hanumān words in accord with dharma.
t.6.101.30: Who would be angry, O best of monkeys, with maidservants who are obedient and subject to the king on whom they depend, and who act only at another's command?
t.6.101.31: Through the working of adverse fortune and through misdeeds done in the past, all this has befallen me; for what one has done oneself is surely what one comes to experience.
t.6.101.32: "It was certain that this had to be undergone by me through the working of my fate; weak as I am, I forgive the female servants of Rāvaṇa here."
t.6.101.33: Commanded by Rāvaṇa, these rākṣasīs threatened me. Now that he is slain, they would surely not make threats, O best of monkeys.
t.6.101.34: Hear from me, O monkey, this ancient verse, imbued with dharma, which was sung by a bear in the presence of a tiger.
t.6.101.35: A superior person does not take up the evil of others who do evil; the rule of conduct must be guarded, for the good have good conduct as their ornament.
t.6.101.36: Whether they are wicked or virtuous, or even deserving of death, O monkey, compassion should be shown by a noble person, for there is no one who never transgresses.
t.6.101.38: Thus addressed by Sītā, Hanumān, skilled in speech, then replied to Sītā, the illustrious wife of Rāma.
t.6.101.37: Nothing ignoble should be done even to rākṣasas who take any form at will and delight in harming the world, even while they are committing evil deeds.
t.6.101.39: You, the illustrious lawful wife of Rāma, are truly worthy of him. Give me your message in reply, O queen; I shall go to where Rāghava is.
t.6.101.40: Thus addressed by Hanumān, Vaidehī, the daughter of Janaka, said: "O best of monkeys, I wish to see my husband."
t.6.101.41: Having heard those words of hers, Hanumān, the son of the Wind, of great splendor, spoke these words, gladdening Maithilī.
t.6.101.42: O noble lady, you will behold Rāma, whose face is like the full moon, together with Lakṣmaṇa, he whose friends stand firm and whose enemies are slain, just as Śacī beholds the lord of the thirty gods.
t.6.101.43: Having thus spoken to Sītā, who shone like Śrī herself made manifest, Hanūmān of great swiftness came to where Rāghava was.
